explain.say: Have you ever sat in the playground and felt like nobody noticed you? That empty feeling is loneliness, and almost everyone feels it sometimes. Look at the board: why do we feel lonely? First, humans need people.

explain.say: Look at these ideas: say hello to one person, join a club, call family, or help someone. Small steps work best. Well done! If loneliness lasts a long time, tell a trusted grown-up or a school counsellor. Challenge: say hi to someone new this week.

steps.note: Talk to someone who loves you

faq.q: Why do humans need other people?
faq.a: For most of history, people survived by living and working in groups. So our brains are built to feel safer and happier when we are connected to others.

faq.q: Can you feel lonely with people around you?
faq.a: Yes. Loneliness is about feeling understood and connected, not about how many people are nearby. You can feel lonely in a busy classroom and happy alone in your room.
asks: Why do I feel lonely at school?

faq.q: What can I do when I feel lonely?
faq.a: Try a small step: say hello to someone, join a club or team, call a family member, or help someone. Talking to a trusted grown-up about the feeling helps too.
asks: How do I stop feeling lonely?

faq.q: Is it bad to like being on my own?
faq.a: Not at all. Alone time can be restful and creative. Loneliness is different: it is when you want to feel connected and do not.
asks: Is it weird to like being alone?

faq.q: What if loneliness does not go away?
faq.a: If you feel lonely most of the time for weeks, tell a trusted grown-up, a school counsellor or a doctor. They can help you find ways to connect.

facts: In 2018 the United Kingdom appointed a Minister for Loneliness, and Japan created a similar post in 2021.
A 2020 study at MIT found that after a day alone, people's brains reacted to pictures of others much as hungry brains react to pictures of food.
